pending_interview.category: Martech/AI-product — personalization architecture, attribution modeling, GenAI content pipelines, measurement under privacy constraints
pending_interview.question: You're working with a large retail brand that runs personalized email and paid social campaigns. They've recently built a generative AI content pipeline — meaning an automated system that uses a large language model to draft and vary ad copy at scale — and they want to tie it into their attribution model (the system that tracks which marketing touchpoints led to a purchase). Their problem: browser privacy changes and the deprecation of third-party cookies (small tracking files that used to let advertisers follow users across websites) have degraded the accuracy of their multi-touch attribution data by roughly 40%. The CMO wants to know which AI-generated content variants are actually driving revenue, not just clicks, in this privacy-constrained environment. How would you redesign their measurement approach, and what tradeoffs would you flag to the CMO between accuracy, scalability, and privacy compliance?
